quarterly_data.quarter: Denka results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Financial Results Presentation Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the Middle East raw-material procurement restrictions: the initial fiscal-2026 forecast assumed a negative JPY 5.0 billion operating-income impact from reduced production; acetylene black made in Singapore was expected to be hit until the end of September and, with the outlook uncertain, that impact could exceed the initial forecast, but other products have not been significantly affected, so the company now expects around half of the JPY 5.0 billion impact to materialize. The Singapore acetylene black is mainly used in high-voltage cables and can be substituted with supply from the Omuta Plant, whose capacity is limited; the company has yet to confirm whether supplier factories are back in operation.
quarterly_data.figure: about half of the JPY 5.0 billion initial impact now expected

quarterly_data.quarter: Denka results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Financial Results Presentation Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on soft-type SNECTON for copper clad laminates (CCL): the shortage of low-dielectric glass cloth, a CCL raw material, is a risk for some users planning to launch next-generation grades, but glass cloth from Taiwanese and Chinese manufacturers is being adopted by a growing number of users, so the company expects production of CCL incorporating this glass cloth to launch at around the end of 2026 and soft-type SNECTON to be adopted by users in a phased manner in 2027 and beyond. For hard-type SNECTON, where many competing resins exist, Denka will narrow its focus to applications that leverage its low CTE and superior dimensional stability.
quarterly_data.figure: CCL with alternative glass cloth around end of 2026; soft-type SNECTON phased adoption in 2027 and beyond

quarterly_data.quarter: Denka results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Financial Results Presentation Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the low-dielectric organic filler under development: it is expected to replace PTFE filler in modified polyimide (MPI)-based flexible CCL (FCCL) because it is PFAS-free, and can be combined with inorganic fillers in rigid CCL to reduce the dielectric constant (Dk); Denka cites its ability to make both organic and inorganic fillers and plans to expand applications to include, for example, resin-based interposers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Denka results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Financial Results Presentation Q&A (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on other items: inventory effects for the first half are expected to total approximately JPY 6.0 billion (positive inventory effects at the December-year Singapore subsidiary's resin products in its second quarter likely offset by negative effects from lower raw-material prices); chloroprene rubber (CR) sales rose on upfront demand in Q1 with a recoil weakening demand in Q2, but full-year CR sales volume is forecast to meet plan; for Life Innovation, second-half rapid antigen test kit sales may fall short of forecasts as in the first half because infectious diseases are not prevalent, the outlook is unclear, and forecasts will be reviewed at the first-half results.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 inventory effects approximately JPY 6.0 billion
